newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Far East looks to Navy for winter warmth.
newsitem.headline: Russian Far East looks to Navy for winter warmth.

text.p: The Russian Far East is running short of fuel and has asked the navy for help with its latest energy crisis, local officials said on Thursday.
The press office of Vladivostok mayor Viktor Cherepkov said the Pacific city had fuel stocks to keep power turbines running for just two days.

A spokesman said Cherepkov and the local Pacific Fleet were discussing how to transfer fuel supplies from the fleet's depot to the city. He said Moscow had not fulfilled October promises to help the region with fuel supplies.
A strike by power workers demanding payment of millions of dollars of back wages froze parts of the Far Eastern region in late September, forcing Moscow to promise aid.
Cherepkov also wanted the autonomous district of Yakutia, to the north, and other regions neighboring the Pacific Primorsky Krai to supply the region with electricity or fuel, he said.
Interfax news agency said the mayor of a small coastal town, Bolshoi Kamen, had told the city's 30,000 residents to prepare for evacuation when fuel supplies ran out on November 25.
Vladivostok, which backed President Boris Yeltsin during his July re-election, was a major participant in a nationwide day of action to protest at unpaid wages earlier this month.
It has been hard hit by cash and power shortages among local industries, especially in the defence and coal sectors.
